architecture.approach: Add six independent crates under crates/* without touching the root manifest or CI. ffscene compiles a validated scene into a deterministic FFmpeg filter graph and argument vector; mixbus processes interleaved f32 blocks through a pre-allocated plan with a bounded command queue and lock-free meter snapshots; replay-recorder writes already-encoded packets into isolated spool tracks with segment, tee, and ring sinks behind a hard disk budget; studio-protocol defines a JSON envelope, messages, role permissions, and a pure state machine; rtmp-publish models RTMP, RTMPS, SRT, and WHIP destinations with redaction by construction, shape validation, shallow probes, bounded retry, a circuit breaker, and failover; signedlink signs claims with HMAC-SHA256, issues base62 codes, normalises UTM parameters, carries an attribution window, and requires a LinkStore for revocation and single use. A final phase enforces metadata, examples, feature independence, lints, rustdoc, packaging, and the security baseline. Publication to crates.io is a post-merge action from main.

dataModel.flowDescription: Scene data flows from app memory into ffscene validation and compilation and out as arguments and labels; audio frames flow caller -> mixbus plan -> caller, with meters read from a separate snapshot; encoded packets flow caller -> replay-recorder -> spool files and index; protocol messages flow JSON -> studio-protocol decode -> version, permission, ordering, budget checks -> pure transition -> new StudioState; destinations flow config -> rtmp-publish validation -> probe -> retry and breaker state -> health and bitrate hint; link claims flow signer -> canonical bytes -> HMAC token -> signed URL, then back through verify -> store -> claims or a typed rejection. No crate owns a database; only replay-recorder writes durable files, and only behind validated IDs and a disk budget.

securityConsiderations.description: SecretString and SigningKey implement Debug and Display by hand and do not implement Serialize; signature tokens are redacted; the RedactedDestination is the only serialisable destination view.
CON-511 authentication: keys are caller-supplied and validated for presence and shape; signedlink verification fails closed; a missing stream key is InvalidKey.
CON-512 authorization: studio-protocol checks permissions before every transition; signedlink revocation and single use are store-enforced.
CON-514 rate limiting: rtmp-publish bounds retries and breaker transitions; studio-protocol enforces the 50 msg/s per-participant budget.
CON-515 input validation: every public entry point validates and returns a typed error; no unwrap on untrusted input.
CON-516 injection protection: spool paths derive from validated newtypes; no SQL or Redis backend ships; the LinkStore contract documents parameterised access.
CON-519 environment security: no .env files, no committed keys, and no embedded credentials; keys are arguments.
CON-520 HTTPS/HSTS: probes and redirects use TLS-capable schemes, plaintext WHIP is rejected, and HSTS is documented as an edge responsibility.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Sort and normalise before emission, use ordered collections, and never embed timestamps or process identity in the graph.
Pre-allocate at maximum block size, use a fixed-capacity command queue, and swap plans atomically at a block boundary.
Check the budget before opening a segment and periodically during writes; bound segment size and delete partial files immediately.
Use a fixed per-participant window with O(1) work per message and no unbounded queue.
Bounded exponential backoff with a cap and O(1) breaker transitions.

risks.description: Six crates in one feature create a large review unit.
risks.mitigation: Independent phases, each leaving the workspace compiling; review per phase.

risks.description: Real-time audio guarantees are hard to prove.
risks.mitigation: Fixed buffers, bounded queue, atomic plan swap, and an aborting-allocator test from /sdrive:test.

risks.description: FFmpeg filter syntax changes across versions.
risks.mitigation: Target FFmpeg 7.x, use golden files, and document the dialect boundary.

risks.description: A stream key leaks through a derived type or tracing field.
risks.mitigation: Redaction by construction, no Serialize for secrets, and a property test over key formats.

risks.description: Disk-budget enforcement races with concurrent writers.
risks.mitigation: Single writer per track, pre-write checks, and atomic index rename.

risks.description: Permission checks drift from the message table.
risks.mitigation: One table, one check call site, and a matrix test.

risks.description: Dependency additions raise MSRV or pull a runtime.
risks.mitigation: Optional and feature-gated dependencies plus the existing MSRV job.

risks.description: signedlink is mistaken for a stateless revocable link system.
risks.mitigation: Require the store for revocation and single use and document the boundary.

risks.description: Code duplication across crates for IDs, errors, and redaction.
risks.mitigation: Keep each crate single-purpose and accept small documented duplication instead of a framework crate (CON-103).

risks.description: Scope creep into M5 providers or platform-core.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the out-of-scope list; later work becomes a new feature or version.
